target.title: fix(qqbot): add timeout to speech transcription requests
target.body:
Related: #95865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot voice-message handling could wait indefinitely when the configured STT endpoint accepts the transcription request but never responds.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot already bounds adjacent API and media requests; this change passes a resolved STT request deadline into `fetchWithSsrFGuard` while preserving the existing response body caps. The runtime now uses existing public provider/media timeout configuration paths instead of introducing unsupported direct `channels.qqbot.stt.timeout*` keys.

## User Impact

Voice-message processing now fails within a bounded timeout instead of blocking the QQBot inbound attachment path on a stalled STT provider request.

## Evidence

- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/stt.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/config.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/manifest-schema.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 28 passed (28)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/stt.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/stt.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/config-schema.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.
- Mutation check: temporarily removing `timeoutMs: sttCfg.timeoutMs` made the focused hanging-server Vitest remain pending instead of rejecting; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: QQBot STT transcription requests now have a deadline when the server accepts the request but never responds.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that accepts the connection and never responds, driving the real exported `resolveSTTConfig` and `transcribeAudio` paths through the SSRF-guarded fetch boundary.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/stt.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/config.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/manifest-schema.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused tests show provider `models.providers.openai.timeoutSeconds: 45` resolves to `45_000`, then use a real loopback hanging STT endpoint with provider `timeoutSeconds: 1`; the mocked SSRF guard honors the passed `timeoutMs: 1000`, receives the real POST, and `transcribeAudio` rejects with a timeout-class error instead of remaining pending. Config and manifest-schema tests confirm no unsupported direct QQBot STT timeout keys were added.

Observed result after fix: `Test Files 3 passed (3)` and `Tests 28 passed (28)`.

What was not tested: live QQ platform traffic or a live third-party STT provider; the hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.

target.title: improve(android): manage configured model providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Android users could only see provider readiness summaries in Settings > Providers & Models, without a clear list of provider-configured model IDs or direct controls to verify, add, or remove provider model definitions.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a provider-model management path for the Android app. The screen now loads a provider-configured model view, expands each provider to show its model IDs, and exposes model availability checks plus add/remove controls.

The review surfaced a source-of-truth risk: the existing `models.list` configured view can be affected by `agents.defaults.models` allowlists, while add/remove operations write `models.providers.*.models`. This update fixes that by adding a source-aware `models.list` view, `provider-config`, and making Android management use that view. The normal picker-style `configured` view keeps its existing allowlist behavior.

Follow-up review also surfaced an Android code-quality issue: the shared Android `modelCatalog` state was being reused by both normal picker/health consumers and the Providers & Models management screen. This update splits the Android state so:

- `modelCatalog` remains the normal configured picker/catalog view.
- `providerModelCatalog` is dedicated to Settings > Providers & Models and uses `view: "provider-config"`.

That keeps the management source of truth aligned without changing unrelated Android model consumers.

Model configuration writes are handled by `models.configure` and `models.remove` gateway RPC methods that operate on `snapshot.sourceConfig`, not the runtime-expanded config. That keeps Android from accidentally persisting bundled/default runtime model catalog entries when adding or removing one model.

## User Impact

Android users can now:

- View provider-configured model providers and detailed model IDs under each provider.
- Refresh provider/model availability from Gateway.
- Check whether an individual model is currently available from the Gateway catalog/readiness view.
- Add or update a provider-configured model ID without editing config files manually.
- Remove an authored provider model with a confirmation dialog.

## Evidence

Code/test coverage added:

- Android UI/state tests in `ProviderModelStatusTest` for provider model rows, availability readiness, and model-test result keys.
- Gateway handler tests in `config.shared-auth.test.ts` proving `models.configure` and `models.remove` write only authored provider models and do not persist runtime-only default catalog entries.
- Gateway model-list tests proving `models.list` `provider-config` returns provider-authored rows even when `agents.defaults.models` allowlists exist, and does not show allowlist-only models.
- Protocol validation coverage for `models.list` `view: "provider-config"`.
- Explicit method-scope assertions for `models.configure` and `models.remove` as `operator.admin` methods.
- Updated native Android i18n source inventory for the new strings.
- Updated gateway/model docs to document `configured` vs `provider-config` semantics.

Local lightweight checks:

- `pnpm native:i18n:check` passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.ts src/gateway/server.models-voicewake-misc.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

GitHub Actions on PR #101912 / source head `47bc07434b1275d53555d7c96b4a91b507d0cc89`:

- `Real behavior proof` passed.
- `android-build-play` passed.
- `android-ktlint` passed.
- `android-test-play` passed.
- `android-test-third-party` passed.
- `check-lint` passed.
- `check-test-types` passed.
- `native-i18n` passed.
- `check-prod-types` passed.
- Security, dependency guard, label, docs, compact/QA, and critical quality checks reported passing/skipped as applicable.

## Real behavior proof

Real Android UI/media proof was captured from `snowzlmbot/openclaw` GitHub Actions, not from a local emulator and not from source/static screenshots.

- Proof workflow run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/28918884394
- Source PR head built by proof workflow: `47bc07434b1275d53555d7c96b4a91b507d0cc89`
- Artifact: `pr-101912-real-android-models-media-proof-47bc07434b1275d53555d7c96b4a91b507d0cc89`
- Artifact id: `8158784255`
- Artifact size: ~3.0 MB
- Artifact expires: 2026-08-07
- Artifact contents: real emulator PNG screenshots, UIAutomator XML dumps, ADB screenrecord MP4, Android logcat, proof gateway request log, and manifest.

What the media proof demonstrates:

1. The workflow checks out PR head `android-models-management-20260708` at `47bc07434b1275d53555d7c96b4a91b507d0cc89` and builds the debug APK in GitHub Actions.
2. GitHub Actions starts an Android emulator and installs the APK.
3. The app connects through its real Android `GatewaySession` WebSocket path to a local proof gateway.
4. The real UI opens Settings > Providers & Models.
5. The screen displays provider-configured model IDs from a live `models.list` request with `view: "provider-config"`.
6. Tapping Test triggers `models.list` with `view: "all"` and captures the visible Available state.
7. Tapping Remove captures the real confirmation dialog and sends `models.remove`.
8. Typing provider/model/name and tapping Save sends `models.configure`, and the real UI captures the added model row.

The downloaded proof artifact was inspected before updating this PR. Its gateway request log contains `models.list` with `provider-config`, `models.list` with `all`, `models.remove`, and `models.configure`; its UI XML/screenshots show the Providers & Models screen, `proof-model-alpha`, the Remove confirmation dialog, the remove-applied state, and `proof-added-model` after save.

Not run locally:

- Android Gradle build/ktlint/test suites were not used as final local evidence; full Android validation and media capture were performed by GitHub Actions above.

Additional note:

- Local graphify rebuild was attempted after code edits. It reached AST extraction completion but did not cleanly exit within the local timeout; no `graphify-out` files are tracked in this PR.
